thread:
alex: seeing a sudden p95/p99 spike for hosted API around 18:05 UTC, started ~1749994300, any quick surface-level ideas?

maria: yep noticed. stack: serving-runtime v3.2.1, kernel-selector bumped in last rollout.

shane: traffic pattern looks weird — a bunch of mid-length requests (~450 tokens) that all hit cold KV cache keys. queue depth on hostpool-7 jumped.

samir: can you paste the top counters? especially kvcache.miss, coalescer.delay, batch.size histo.

alex: pasted counters: `kvcache.miss = +12x`, `coalescer.delay_p50 = 42ms -> 210ms`, `batch.size_p95 = 1 -> 4`

cheng: that suggests many small batches and KV priming blocking the sampler. might be lockstep prefetch from same tenant.

maria: tenant trace for tenant-422 attached: 90% of requests triggered `kv.prefetch(serial)` paths, priming latency ~180ms, and we saw kernel-selector pick aux-kernel (slower quantized path) for ~30% of requests.

shane: aux-kernel pick is odd — selector should favor fast kernel for seq<512. profiler shows kernel-metrics spike at the same time as kvcache misses.

samir: hypothesis: rate-limiter burst boundary + deterministic prefetch ordering -> many concurrent priming ops serialized on the same backend lock, causing queue lockstep and forcing kernel fallback due to sampler timing out.

alex: runtime-bot: created perf-record 1749994348 with flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/1749994348

runtime-bot: alert: hostpool-7 node3 CPU steal high during window, but GPU utilization steady.

cheng: CPU steal implies system-level scheduling interference — could exacerbate priming latencies that run on CPU threads (IO + decompression).

maria: check kernel selector logs: `selector.trace` shows several `fallback_to_aux` events at 1749994330-1749994360 for tenant-422.

shane: I can repro locally with a script that fires parallel requests with same prefix keys; it triggers KV priming and queue backpressure. gist: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s ... & done` with identical prompt.

samir: steps we tried in prod canary: 1) reduce prefetch concurrency for hosted tier from 8 -> 2, 2) add jitter to prefetch order, 3) bump per-tenant token rate limit by 10% to smooth bursts. results: p95 dropped ~65ms in canary.

alex: we also rolled kernel-selector to previous heuristic (disable aggressive fallback) on canary and saw fallback events drop from 30% -> 4%.

maria: note: disabling aggressive fallback increases risk of headroom miss for very long sequences; tracking that in canary.

cheng: additional observation: coalescer had a starvation window because many requests stayed singleton while KV priming held sampler thread. patch idea: make KV priming async and allow coalescer to proceed with partial cached state (serve best-effort).

samir: quick mitigation deployed to hosted canary: `prefetch.max_concurrency=2`, `prefetch.jitter_enabled=true`, `selector.aggressive_fallback=false` at 1749994450.

runtime-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout succeeded on 3/3 hosts for pool hostpool-7-canary at 1749994462 

alex: post-mitigation metrics look better: kvcache.miss rate normalized, p95 down, batch sizes increased slightly (more coalescing).

shane: long-term actions: (1) async prefetch path + circuit-breaker, (2) selector telemetry refinement (use seq-dist histo per-tenant), (3) experiment with per-tenant priming backoff.

maria: I've opened tasks: RED-ops #1124 (async prefetch design), RED-telemetry #778 (selector per-tenant histo), RED-runtime #1199 (coalescer improvement). Assigned: maria, cheng, samir.

infra-oncall: also we saw ephemeral IO congestion on node3 around the time window — infra will follow up on host-level IO priority scheduling.

alex: thanks all. keeping thread pinned. will monitor for 24h and then schedule postmortem if reoccurs. :thumbsup:

cheng: quick note: add a short-lived alert for `kvcache.miss_ratio > 7% && coalescer.delay_p95 > 150ms` so we catch similar lockstep earlier.

samir: 👍 added alert in grafana (RED-alarms #55).

alex: ok closing the immediate triage, will update if anything new pops up.
